m1_zero_omission_notes.summary: This chapter investigates geometric line relationships on plane surfaces, including intersecting lines, point of intersection, vertically opposite angles, linear pairs, perpendicular lines, and parallel lines. Concepts are explored through paper folding activities and formal geometric proofs.

detailed_sections.full_notes:
Two distinct lines on a plane intersect at at most one point. When two lines intersect, four angles are formed. Key properties:
1. Vertically Opposite Angles are equal: angle a = angle c and angle b = angle d.
2. Linear Pairs: Adjacent angles on a straight line add up to 180 degrees (supplementary): angle a + angle b = 180, angle b + angle c = 180.

margin_notes.title: Uniqueness of Intersection
margin_notes.content: Two non-coincident straight lines can never intersect at more than one point.

detailed_sections.full_notes: Parallel lines lie in the same plane and never intersect, no matter how far extended in either direction. The perpendicular distance between parallel lines is constant throughout. Perpendicular lines intersect at right angles (90 degrees).

margin_notes.title: Grid Identification
margin_notes.content: Identify parallel line pairs drawn on dot grid paper.

detailed_sections.full_notes: Folding a square paper in half creates a crease parallel to top/bottom edges. Subsequent parallel folds double the number of parallel line segments created. Folding perpendicular to horizontal creases forms a grid of right angles.

margin_notes.title: Crease Patterns
margin_notes.content: Horizontal folds produce parallel creases; vertical folds produce perpendicular creases.

m3_practical_activities_and_procedures.activity_title: Paper Folding to Construct Parallel & Perpendicular Lines
m3_practical_activities_and_procedures.aim: To construct parallel and perpendicular line creases using square paper folding
procedure: Fold paper in half horizontally to make crease L1.
Fold in half again horizontally to make creases L2, L3.
Unfold and observe that all horizontal creases are parallel.
Fold vertically in half to create crease P1 perpendicular to L1, L2, L3.
m3_practical_activities_and_procedures.observation_and_conclusion: Successive parallel folds create multiple parallel lines. Vertical fold creates perpendicular lines to all horizontal creases.

end_exercises.question: Can two straight lines intersect at more than one point?
end_exercises.answer: No. Two distinct straight lines can intersect at most at one unique point.

level_2_short_answer_2_3_marks.question: Two intersecting lines form angle x and angle y as a linear pair. If x = 2y, find x and y.
level_2_short_answer_2_3_marks.answer: Linear pair sum: x + y = 180°. Substitute x = 2y: 2y + y = 180° => 3y = 180° => y = 60°. Then x = 2(60°) = 120°.

level_3_long_answer_5_marks.question: In an intersection of two straight lines, four angles a, b, c, d are formed in clockwise order. If a = 35°, find b, c, and d with full mathematical reasons.
level_3_long_answer_5_marks.answer:
1. angle a and angle b form a linear pair: a + b = 180° => 35° + b = 180° => b = 145°.
2. angle c is vertically opposite to angle a: c = a = 35°.
3. angle d is vertically opposite to angle b: d = b = 145°.
Results: b = 145°, c = 35°, d = 145°.

level_4_competency_case_study.scenario: Architects design a window grid where vertical frame line V is perpendicular to horizontal sill line H. Diagonal support brace D crosses the intersection at 35° to line H.

qa.question: Find all four angles formed between support brace D and horizontal sill line H.
qa.answer: Angle 1 = 35°. Angle 2 (linear pair) = 180° - 35° = 145°. Angle 3 (vertically opposite to 1) = 35°. Angle 4 (vertically opposite to 2) = 145°.

m7_common_pitfalls.common_error: Assuming any two non-intersecting line segments in a bounded drawing are parallel.
m7_common_pitfalls.correct_approach: Line segments must remain equidistant when extended infinitely to be truly parallel.
